reason: E2 directly supports the coating method, protective oxide formation, and oxidation resistance on a refractory HEA, but only at 800 °C and without quantitative weight gain or adhesion data. E1 shows Cr reduces weight gain on a different alloy system at 800 °C, but does not involve silicide coatings or the specific alloy class. premises: A Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating can be applied to refractory high-entropy alloys via a fused slurry method.
The silicide coating forms a protective oxide layer (primarily SiO2) during high-temperature oxidation.
The coating reduces oxidation weight gain and improves scale adhesion compared to uncoated alloys.
The coating is effective under isothermal oxidation in air at 800–900 °C for ~50 hours.
Cr addition in high-entropy alloys improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
